card.name: The word orally after a dose
card.fires_on: The word "orally" right after a dose amount such as "5 mg" or "taken", in dosing instructions, just before a frequency like "twice daily".

modes.label: Orally after taken
modes.description: "orally" follows "mg taken" in a recommended-dose sentence.
modes.example: The recommended dose of ELIQUIS for most patients is 5 mg taken<< orally>> twice daily.

modes.label: Orally straight after mg
modes.description: "orally" comes directly after the milligram amount, with no verb in between.
modes.example: The recommended dosage of nilotinib capsules is 400 mg<< orally>> twice daily.

card.writes: It seems to push toward number-like or count-like words and to hold back small number words such as five or six.
card.plain: It lights up on the word "orally" when a label gives a dose and is about to say how often.
evidence: The recommended dose of ELIQUIS for most patients is 5 mg taken<< orally>> twice daily.
